identity.name: Priya Raghunathan
identity.headline: Principal Engineer, Distributed Systems
identity.tagline: Fifteen years making large systems boring, on purpose.

bio.short: Principal engineer working on storage and consensus. I like systems that fail in ways you can explain to someone at 3am.
bio.long: I have spent most of my career on the unglamorous half of distributed systems: replication, durability, and the long tail of failure modes that only show up at scale. Before that I wrote compilers, which turned out to be excellent preparation for reasoning about ordering. These days I split my time between platform work, mentoring, and writing about the operational side of the job that rarely makes it into papers.

projects.title: Quorum
projects.summary: An open-source Raft implementation with a deterministic simulation test suite.
projects.description: Quorum grew out of frustration with consensus bugs that only reproduced under load. The whole cluster runs inside a single-threaded deterministic scheduler, so a failing seed reproduces byte for byte on any machine. It has found ordering bugs that ran in production for years.

projects.title: Ledger Migration
projects.summary: Moved a 40TB financial ledger between storage engines with no downtime.
projects.description: An eighteen-month dual-write and reconciliation programme across six teams, ending in a cutover that took four minutes and needed no rollback.

projects.title: Sift
projects.summary: Log search that stays cheap by refusing to index anything you never query.

projects.title: Failure Atlas
projects.summary: A public catalogue of distributed-systems failure modes and their tells.

experience.summary: Technical direction for the storage platform behind every customer-facing product.
highlights: Led the ledger migration: 40TB moved with a four-minute cutover.
Cut p99 write latency by 62% by reworking the replication path.
Established the design review practice now used across engineering.

experience.summary: Consensus and replication for a multi-region key-value store.
highlights: Shipped multi-region replication to 400+ enterprise clusters.
Built the deterministic test harness that became Quorum.

experience.summary: Optimisation passes and instruction selection for an in-house DSL.

education.note: Thesis on speculative execution in dataflow runtimes.
